beats.spoken: In the EU, your sunscreen's UVA protection should be at least a third of its SPF.

The European Commission has recommended this since 2006. Sunscreens should protect well enough against both UVB and UVA radiation, so that public health is properly protected. Claims about UVA and UVB protection should only be made if these minimum levels are met.
The recommendation sets minimum values. UVB protection should reach at least SPF 6. The UVA protection factor should be at least one third of the SPF on the label. So for SPF 30, at least 10.

Then there's the critical wavelength. It should be at least 370 nanometres. It describes how far the protection reaches into the UVA range. The recommendation notes that dermatologists recommend this value.
Today, UVA protection can be measured with the ISO 24443 standard. It describes a lab test that gives, among other things, the UVA protection factor and the critical wavelength.
For you, that means: the SPF is only half the story. Check that your sunscreen also states its UVA protection.
